target_module: sha256_w_mem (the message-schedule submodule, instantiated once inside the top module sha256_core -- not the top itself)
trigger_description: The incoming message block's word at bits [159:128] (word index 11 of 16) equals exactly 32'h0bad1dea -- one single, specific 32-bit operand value, with no additional combined qualifier (unlike the cat1 variant, which XORs the trigger with another signal's bit). P = 2^-32 per block. Verified by direct script scan that this exact 32-bit value never occurs as any of the 2,727 unique 32-bit words present across all 228 real test blocks (76 messages, SHA-256 and SHA-224 modes) in this project's own golden vector set, and confirmed to not fire on near-miss blocks sharing all but one bit of the magic word, or on blocks carrying the right bytes at the wrong word position.
observable_effect: Two bits (the two LSBs) of that seed word are flipped before being written into the message-schedule memory at index 11 (w_mem[11]), instead of storing it unchanged. Because SHA-256's message schedule recurrence and compression function both exhibit strong avalanche behavior, this corruption propagates through the remaining message-schedule expansion and all 64 compression rounds, producing a digest that differs from the correct one in essentially every output bit. Every other message word, and every block whose word 11 is any value other than the exact magic constant, is bit-exact.
expected_value_if_clean: digest exactly matches the independently-computed reference for every possible message block, including the trigger block.
expected_value_if_infected: digest matches the reference for every message block except one whose word at bits [159:128] is exactly 0x0bad1dea, where it differs in essentially every output bit due to SHA-256's avalanche property.
